reason: This and wordmark-first-baseline-drifts-22px-on-timeline are ONE defect reported twice — same span.word, same cause (--stage-pad top plus --lead-body), same widths, differing only in datum (optical centre vs first baseline) — and the identity-drops-on-the-timeline-crossing reasoning kills both: measured at the wordmark's own left, the only two boxes aligned below Timeline's mark are div.tl-stage and section.b-field, so its 40px top is the same page inset as its 40px left, exactly as Tasks' mark sits on the 28px its trayHead/trayTop/pip/segItem resolve to and Notes' sits on the stack's own edge. The centres reproduce (30.00 / 31.01 / 52.75 at 1920 and 1440), but the alignment being defended is not a contract: driven at six widths the Tasks-Notes gap is 0.13px at 1920 and 1440, 0.87px at 1280 and 1100, 10.95px at 768, and 5.87px at 390 — where Timeline's wordmark already sits 8px ABOVE Tasks', so raising it makes the phone worse. And the finding's premise that this is 'the one object nailed to the sheet' is contradicted by its own concession: Notes' wordmark stands 371px from the sheet edge at 1920, 131 at 1440, 51 at 1280, 16 at 390, a 355px horizontal slide the finding calls defensible. The fix is also unwritable as specified: var(--lead-tight) exists in neither timeline.css nor across.css, and Timeline's declared ladder (0.9 / 1.06 / 1.2 / 1.3 / 1.4 / 1.5, 'six steps... audit.mjs fails a leading that is not one of them') has no step yielding a 22px box at 17px.
